question: Should RFC 0018 be accepted with required/advisory conditions, activation-scoped plugin provider registration, and explicit `gateway.readiness` criteria selection as the v1 contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but choosing a permanent readiness model, public plugin API, and new configuration surface is product and compatibility policy that cannot be inferred from tests or implementation proof.

options.title: Accept the proposed v1
options.body: Approve the three contract choices, create the implementation issue, update the lifecycle metadata, and proceed with compatibility review of the linked runtime PR.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Accept canonical core conditions first while deferring plugin providers or operator-selected criteria to a later RFC revision.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft or close it until maintainers want to commit to an extensible readiness API and support contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the proposed v1
recommendation.body: Approve the three contract choices, create the implementation issue, update the lifecycle metadata, and proceed with compatibility review of the linked runtime PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history spans both Gateway lifecycle behavior and plugin runtime surfaces, which are the two principal contract boundaries requiring a decision.
